Peterborough and Cambridgeshire |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c62dezn93pdo |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=BBC News |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Hannah |date=2026-01-22 |title=The 3 Cambridgeshire areas where elections will go ahead this year |url=https://www.cambridge-news.co.uk/news/local-news/government-confirms-elections-held-cambridgeshire-33283498 |access-date=2026-01-29 |website=Cambridgeshire Live |language=en}} This was on the same day as other [[2026 UK local elections|local elections]]. Due to ongoing [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|local government reorganisation]], this is the final election to Cambridge City Council before it is abolished and replaced by a successor [[unitary authority]]. Elections to the successor authority are due to take place in 2027. ==Background== In [[2024 Cambridge City Council election|2024]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] retained control of the council.{{Cite web |last=Brown |first=Hannah |date=3 May 2024 |title=Cambridge City Council local election 2024 results breakdown in full |url=https://www.cambridge-news.co.uk/news/cambridge-news/cambridge-city-council-local-election-29094246 |access-date=29 January 2026 |website=Cambridgeshire Live |language=en}}{{Cite news |title=Cambridge result - Local Elections 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/election/2024/england/councils/E07000008 |access-date=29 January 2026 |work=[[BBC News]] |language=en-GB}} ===Council composition=== {| class="wikitable" |- ! colspan="3" | After 2024 election ! colspan="3" | Before 2026 election |- ! colspan="2" | Party !
